ns_police.text: Republic of Cyprus police. Crossing north? Passport or ID card, please. You'll show it again on the other side.
From here it's a few steps through the buffer zone. The UN has the bit in the middle. Nobody has the pigeons.

then.text: Go on, over the line. The hellim seller in the Büyük Han will tell you the same, only louder.
Andreas and Hüseyin? Still? They've been at this since before you were born.

Here's the truth. It's one cheese, made all over the island by both communities for centuries. In 2021 the EU protected it under two names at once: halloumi and hellim. One cheese, one register, two words.
But don't take it from me. Cross at the top of Ledra Street and ask in the Büyük Han. A verdict needs both sides, or it isn't one.

else.text: Taste both first, love. A judge with one mouthful is just a customer.
Halloumi! Fresh this morning. Grill it, fry it, eat it with watermelon in August, which sounds mad and isn't.

ns_yiayia.text: I was born in Kyrenia, on the north coast. In the summer of 1974 we left with what we could carry. For twenty-nine years I couldn't go back.
When the crossings opened in 2003 I went to see my house. A Turkish Cypriot family lives there. They had lost their own home, near Paphos, in the south. We had coffee. We both cried.
Then we argued about the coffee. We still visit. Her grandson fixed my television.

ns_bureau.text: Euros on this side. If you're crossing north, they mostly use the Turkish lira, though plenty of places take euros at their own rate. Change some here, or there.
